plan.analysis: Only evidence is p0001: constant f gives R=2/3. A quick exact calculation for the monotone ramp f(x)=x already gives R≈0.7736, so asymmetric monotone ramps are the main bet. I will spend one experiment confirming the simple power-law ramp family, one refining it with full-array analytic-gradient local search, and one testing a coarse non-monotone K-block family to see whether monotonicity is actually necessary or whether blocky flat-convolution shapes do better.

experiments.hypothesis: The continuous ramp f(x)=x on [0,1] has R≈0.7736, far above 2/3, and optimizing the exponent in f(x)=x^p should improve it further.
experiments.change: Use N=2000 and x_i=(i+0.5)/N. For each candidate exponent p build h_i=x_i^p (use ones if p=0). Write an exact R(h) evaluator using np.convolve and the given padded-L formula. First evaluate start if present. Then do a coarse logarithmic grid p in [0.05,5] with about 100 values, find the best, and golden-section refine p around it until time.process_time() reaches about 0.85*budget_seconds. If time remains, re-evaluate the best p at N=4000 and N=8000 and keep the best-scoring array. Return the best nonnegative array found.
experiments.prediction: The score will jump above 0.75, probably around 0.77, confirming the ramp mechanism; the optimal p will be finite and near 1 rather than 0 or infinity.

experiments.hypothesis: The power-law ramp is only one monotone shape; full-array local optimization initialized from a ramp can find a better asymmetric monotone profile and push R above 0.78.
experiments.change: Use N=400 and parameterize h=softmax(z). Define q=np.convolve(h,h), L=[0,q,0], B=(sum h)^2, M=max(L), j*=argmax(L), A=(1/3)sum(L_j^2+L_j L_{j+1}+L_{j+1}^2). With c_j=(L_{j-1}+4L_j+L_{j+1})/3 and zero outside, compute for each a: gA_a=2*sum_b c_{a+b+1} h_b, gB_a=2*sum(h), gM_a=2*h[j*-1-a] if 0<=j*-1-a<N else 0. Then gR_a=(gA_a*B*M - A*(gB_a*M+B*gM_a))/(B*M)^2 and dz_a=h_a*(gR_a - sum_b h_b*gR_b). Run scipy.optimize.minimize on -R with method='L-BFGS-B', jac=True, starting from (i) uniform z=0, (ii) the linear ramp z_i=log((i+0.5)/N), and (iii) random low-frequency Fourier perturbations of the best z. Keep restarting from perturbed best until about 0.85*budget_seconds; evaluate start too and return the best h.
experiments.prediction: Result will exceed the plain ramp, with R at least 0.78, and the optimized heights will be monotone increasing or nearly so.

experiments.hypothesis: A nonparametric non-monotone K-block shape may beat the monotone ramp; alternatively, if the global search converges to a monotone ramp, that confirms monotonicity is the key mechanism.
experiments.change: Use N=400 and K=10 equal-width blocks, each 40 steps. Parameterize the block heights as a_k=exp(u_k), k=0..9. Write the exact R evaluator for the expanded 400-step array. Run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on u with bounds [-8,2], popsize=20, tol=0, updating a callback so it stops near 0.80*budget_seconds; then polish the best candidate with coordinate-wise golden-section search or random multiplicative perturbations until 0.85*budget_seconds. Also evaluate start if present. Return the best expanded height array.
experiments.prediction: The block optimum will either be monotone and score about 0.77-0.80, matching the ramp line, or a clearly non-monotone block pattern will score higher, refuting the monotone-ramp bet and opening a new branch.

plan.analysis: p0006's full-array exact-gradient softmax optimization is the strongest line (0.8685). p0007's blocky non-monotone search found a much flatter convolution top but scored slightly lower (0.8662), suggesting its basin may be promising but under-refined. I will (1) refine p0006 at higher resolution, (2) revisit p0007 with full-resolution local optimization, and (3) test a genuinely different search idea that directly encourages a flat convolution peak via a smoothed-max objective annealed to the true max. All experiments must spend the full budget and keep the best exact-R construction found.

experiments.hypothesis: The N=400 discretization limits how finely the optimal shape can be represented; refining the same softmax/L-BFGS optimizer at N=800 and N=1600 should recover a slightly better R.
experiments.change: Take p0006's construction as the start. Upsample it to N=800 by linearly interpolating the step heights at new step midpoints (or repeating values), convert to z=log(h)-mean, and run p0006's exact-gradient softmax L-BFGS-B optimizer at N=800. Then upsample the best N=800 result to N=1600 and repeat. Keep the best exact R among p0006 start, N=800, and N=1600. Use maxiter around 800-1500 and spend the time budget on these refinements.
experiments.prediction: The N=800/1600 refinement will exceed 0.868503 by roughly 0.001-0.005; if it does not, the N=400 shape is already resolution-saturated.

experiments.hypothesis: p0007 found a broad, flat-top convolution maximum but was constrained to 10 log-height blocks. Full 400-step exact-gradient optimization from that non-monotone shape may improve it into a better basin than p0006's sharp-peak solution.
experiments.change: Start from p0007's 400-step construction. Run p0006's existing softmax parameterization h=softmax(z) with the exact analytic gradient of R at N=400, initialized from z=log(start)-mean, using L-BFGS-B with high maxiter. If time remains, upsample the best N=400 result to N=800 and run the same optimizer there. Keep the best exact-R construction seen, including the original p0007 start.
experiments.prediction: p0007's score will rise from 0.8662 to at least ~0.868, and possibly above p0006. If it instead converges to p0006's sharp peak, that confirms p0006's basin is preferred.

experiments.hypothesis: The true max is non-smooth at the argmax, so L-BFGS may settle for a single sharp convolution peak; smoothing the max with a log-sum-exp and annealing beta toward infinity should encourage multiple knots near the maximum and may find a higher-R shape.
experiments.change: Implement a smoothed objective R_beta = A/(B*M_beta), where A and B are as in p0006 and M_beta=(1/beta)*log(sum_j exp(beta*L_j)) over the padded convolution knots, computed stably. Derive its analytic gradient w.r.t. h: reuse p0006's gA and gB; for M_beta, set w_j=softmax(beta*L)_j and compute dM/dh_a = 2*sum_b w_{a+b+1} h_b by correlation, then chain through softmax z. Initialize from p0006's start (upsampled if internal N differs) and anneal beta in stages, e.g. 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, warm-starting L-BFGS between stages. After each stage evaluate exact R and keep the best; finish with a short exact-R L-BFGS polish from the best h.
experiments.prediction: The annealed smoothed-max search will produce a broader near-max plateau and exceed 0.868503, likely reaching 0.87-0.88; if it only matches p0006, the sharp-peak solution is already locally optimal for true R.

plan.analysis: p0011's N=3200 softmax/L-BFGS is the best line (0.868938); resolution gains are nearly exhausted. p0008's flatter convolution top is a genuinely different basin but was only refined to N=1600, so it deserves a high-resolution retest. p0013's smoothed max failed, so I will not repeat that. I bet on (1) low-dimensional Fourier subspace moves to escape p0011's local optimum, (2) carrying p0008 to N=3200 with p0011's exact gradient, and (3) testing whether explicit zero end-support beats the all-positive softmax. Each keeps the best exact-R construction and spends the full budget.

experiments.hypothesis: p0011's high-resolution L-BFGS may be trapped in a local maximum; optimizing a low-dimensional Fourier perturbation of its log-height vector can escape with exact chain-rule gradients, then high-resolution polish can lock in a better basin.
experiments.change: Start from p0011's construction. Upsample to N=3200 if needed, set z0=log(h)-mean. Build a basis B of K=32 sin/cos modes on x_i=(i+0.5)/N (exclude constant). For coefficients a, set z=z0+B a, h=softmax(z), compute p0011's exact R and dz via its _R_and_grad; chain gradient is B.T @ dz. Run L-BFGS-B on a from a=0 and from 10 random a with scale 0.05. After each, reconstruct z and run full N=3200 exact-gradient L-BFGS polish for a limited number of iterations. Keep the best exact-R construction; use all remaining time for more coefficient restarts/polish.
experiments.prediction: R will increase above 0.868938 by roughly 1e-4 to 5e-4; if it does not improve, p0011 is already locally stable under global Fourier modes.

experiments.hypothesis: p0008 found a distinctly flatter convolution top but was only refined to N=1600; running p0011's exact-gradient optimizer at N=3200 from that basin may recover a better non-monotone shape and possibly beat p0011.
experiments.change: Start from p0008's construction. Upsample it to N=3200 by linear interpolation at new step midpoints, convert to z=log(h)-mean, and run p0011's exact-gradient softmax L-BFGS-B at N=3200 with as many iterations as the budget allows. Then, if time remains, add several small random Fourier perturbations to z and re-polish at N=3200. Keep the best exact-R construction at every step.
experiments.prediction: R will exceed p0008's 0.866618, likely landing around 0.868-0.869; if it reaches >0.868938 the flat-top basin is competitive, while convergence to ~0.868938 means the two branches merge.

experiments.hypothesis: The softmax parameterization forces every step height positive; if the true optimum has zero end-support, explicitly trimming tails and reoptimizing the remaining segment can increase R. Conversely, a scan showing alpha=0 is best confirms the all-positive support.
experiments.change: Start from p0011's best construction. For alpha in {0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20}, zero the first floor(alpha*N) and last floor(alpha*N) steps (also try left-only and right-only trims), renormalize, and reoptimize only the nonzero middle segment with p0011's exact-gradient softmax L-BFGS at the same resolution. Keep the best exact-R construction. Use remaining time to refine the best alpha with smaller trim fractions.
experiments.prediction: The best alpha will be 0 or at most 0.02, giving no meaningful gain; a positive improvement from alpha>=0.05 would show that support constraints are limiting p0011.
